author: nickscookingclub
title: Bee Sting Cake Hides Vanilla Cream Beneath Almond Crunch
text:
1 days ago Bee Sting Cake, or Bienenstich, is a German dessert built around three dramatically different textures. A light yeasted cake provides a soft, slightly chewy foundation, which is split and filled with silky vanilla pastry cream lightened with whipped cream. Across the top, a caramelized honey-and-almond glaze bakes into a golden layer that crackles beneath the fork. The cake is sweet without being overwhelming, creamy without becoming heavy, and crunchy enough to make each slice interesting from the first bite to the last.
Photo by Jason Griffith This is an excellent baking project for holidays, brunches, birthdays, or weekends when you want to create something beyond an ordinary frosted cake. Give the yeast enough time to work, cook the pastry cream until properly thickened, and chill the assembled cake so the filling stays neat when sliced. Cutting the almond top into portions before setting it over the cream can make final serving easier and prevent the crisp layer from pressing down on the filling. Toasted honey, vanilla, and buttery almonds give the dessert an old-world bakery aroma while its dramatic cross-section looks completely celebration-ready. It takes planning, but that combination of tender cake, cloudlike cream, and sticky almond crunch provides an unusually satisfying reward.
